body: ## Purpose
How solutions engineers estimate a prospect's monthly tokens before a quote. Estimates use an approximate tokenizer and round up 10% for safety. This page is about forecasting before purchase. It does not explain how billed tokens are counted on an invoice; for that, see the token accounting pages and the billing routing page.
## Method
1. Sample 100 representative requests.
2. Count characters and divide by 4 for English text.
3. Multiply by expected monthly volume and add 10%.

### What counts as “output tokens”
Included:
- Tokens generated by the model and returned to the caller in both streaming and non-streaming responses.
- Tokens generated for tool/function-call structured outputs when they are part of the model’s generated output.
Excluded:
- Input/prompt tokens.
- Tokens generated internally but not returned due to request cancellation, truncation before delivery, or transport errors (unless explicitly flagged as delivered; see “Known limitations”).

content: ## Overview
Some customers reconcile Redwood token usage against internal estimates and may observe higher usage totals. The most common causes are (1) client retries and (2) streaming cancellation behavior.
This page provides a support-ready explanation and recommended mitigations."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/usage-accounting-retries-and-stream-cancellation.json", "chunk": "4/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Usage accounting: retries and streaming cancellation", "status": "published", "date": "2025-02-18", "text": "## Support playbook (quick response blurb)
We record usage per server-admitted attempt. If your client retries after a timeout, each admitted attempt can appear separately in Usage and can be billable. For streaming, prompt tokens are counted once admitted; completion tokens reflect what was generated before cancellation.
## References
- SUP-1842 (Northwind AI escalation)
- INT-330 (UI helper text + KB link)
- Slack #support thread_ts=1739310605"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/tp-timeouts-workaround-dedicated.json", "chunk": "6/14", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Dedicated TP timeouts/hangs under load — temporary mitigations + customer info checklist", "status": "published", "date": "2025-03-03", "text": "### Mitigation C — Streaming guardrails (reduce cancellation-related pathologies)
**When:** Reports mention client disconnects, cancelled requests, mobile clients, or proxy timeouts.
**What to do:**
- Ask the customer to confirm their client behavior: do they cancel streams frequently? Do they enforce aggressive HTTP timeouts?
- Encourage idempotency keys / retry discipline (avoid retry storms)
- If customer controls it: increase client streaming timeouts modestly *only if p99 is close to the timeout* (do not mask stalls)
**Expected outcome:** Reduces incidence of cancel/abort edge cases compounding the stall."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/token-accounting-discrepancy-intake-and-triage.json", "chunk": "4/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Ops: Reconciling token accounting discrepancy reports (intake + triage)", "status": "published", "date": "2025-04-22", "text": "## Known examples (for reference)
- SUP-2841: streaming retry/reconnect behavior leading to perceived token accounting discrepancy
- SUP-2917: embeddings tokenizer mismatch leading to perceived token accounting discrepancy
- SUP-3009: cache-hit + tool calling bug leading to real token accounting discrepancy
## Reporting note
When answering: "Which intake channel has the most reports of token accounting discrepancy?" be sure to include Slack and Gmail-origin cases even if a SUP ticket was created later."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/token-accounting-discrepancy-intake-and-triage.json", "chunk": "2/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Ops: Reconciling token accounting discrepancy reports (intake + triage)", "status": "published", "date": "2025-04-22", "text": "## Definition (use this phrase)
We classify a case as a *token accounting discrepancy* when a customer claims that billed token totals (Console Usage and/or invoice export) do not match their own calculation from application logs or local tokenization.
## Approved intake channels
We track where the report first arrived, because it affects response time and deduplication.
- Jira (customer-support): SUP-* ticket created directly by Support
- Slack: #support threads (often started from Intercom/Zendesk summaries)
- Gmail: finance/billing or CSM forwards to leadership/finance"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-and-comms/incident-communication-templates.json", "chunk": "12/17", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Incident Communication Templates (Status Page + Customer-Facing Updates)", "status": "published", "date": "2026-01-09", "text": "## Product-specific wording guidance
### Hosted API (chat/completions)
Use symptom language customers recognize:
- “elevated 5xx errors”
- “increased request latency”
- “timeouts for completions requests”
Avoid:
- “gateway saturation”
- “scheduler instability”
### Streaming
Streaming issues often look like partial failures.
Preferred symptoms:
- “increased stream disconnects”
- “streaming responses may terminate early”
- “delayed first token” (only if verified)
If non-streaming is unaffected, say so:
"Non-streaming requests are not impacted" (only after verification)."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/streaming-responses-premature-end.json", "chunk": "1/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Known issue: Streaming responses may end prematurely on OpenAI-compatible API", "status": "published", "date": "2025-02-14", "text": "title: Known issue: Streaming responses may end prematurely on OpenAI-compatible API

content: ## Summary
Some customers have reported that streaming responses on Redwood’s OpenAI-compatible API may end early (without the terminal `[DONE]` event). The HTTP status is frequently 200 and the client receives partial tokens before the stream disconnects.
This is most frequently observed in **eu-west** and appears correlated with periods where upstream token generation is temporarily quiet long enough to trigger a gateway read/idle timeout."}]}

{"name": "charge-review", "steps": "Inputs: the developer's org or account id, the invoice (id or month), the lines and amounts they mean, request ids if they have them.

1. Identify the account. If you have neither org nor account id, ask_developer for org_id (plus invoice_id/invoice_month and line_items/amounts/request_ids in the same call if not given). lookup_account.
2. Check the billing channel and plan on the account.
   - Not billed directly by Redwood: search_knowledge for the procedure for that exact channel. A cloud marketplace (aws_marketplace, gcp_marketplace) and a reseller are different channels with different pages; apply only the one matching the console's billing_channel and don't borrow steps from the other. Support usually cannot credit or dispute these; tell the developer who bills them and where adjustments go. Do not open a credit or dispute.
3. Find the invoice: get_invoice (use lookup_account's invoice list to map a month to an id). Read console_confirmed_duplicates and same_amount_but_different_requests. If the developer gave request ids, get_usage them.
4. Classify:
   a. Console-confirmed duplicate: two lines on the same direct invoice billing the identical request ids. The duplicated line is the later line (duplicated_lines); credit that one, never the original.
   b. Look-alike: same amount/description but different request ids, or no second line. NOT a confirmed duplicate: say so plainly, with the console evidence (each line's request ids and times).
   c. Wrong rate/quantity/product, usage they don't recognize, retries/cancelled streams, token-count mismatch: search the token/usage pages first; if they explain it, explain and stop.
   d. Request to waive or reduce a correct charge (goodwill, exception, SLA credit): not Support's to issue. Load team-handoff.
5. For (a), search_knowledge for Support's current credit limit for duplicate charges and how it applies (per line, full line amount, no splitting). Read the approving document's status/date; drafts and proposals do not change the limit. If sources disagree on the limit (e.g. a draft, a thread or the developer cites a different figure), delegate to policy-researcher with the question and the dates before deciding. Compare the duplicated line's full amount with the limit.
   - Within limit: confirm_with_developer "Issue a credit note of $X (reason duplicate) on line L of invoice I". If yes: issue_credit_note for the full line amount with that reason, memo naming the request ids. Tell the developer the credit note id and amount. No handoff needed.
   - Over limit: do not credit and do not split. confirm_with_developer that you will open a dispute on line L and hand it to the owning team. If yes: open_dispute (reason duplicate_charge, the line, the request ids, submit=true), then load team-handoff and escalate with the dispute id.
6. For (b) and unexplained (c): gather intake (invoice, lines, UTC window, request ids, what they checked) with ask_developer, then load team-handoff for the owning team named in the routing policy.
7. Never promise a refund date or dispute outcome. If a write is rejected, read get_invoice to see the state before saying anything."}

This manifests as undercharging for customers and incorrect per-route quota enforcement (routes appear to consume fewer tokens than expected).

- Primary route (route-A) is configured with model M1. Under load, smart routing occasionally falls back to compatible variant M1-quant (or M2-small) to meet latency targets."}, {"source": "sources/linear/engineering/ENG-21849-tokenized-metering-mismatch-fallback-routing.json", "chunk": "2/8", "kind": "Linear issue", "title": "tokenized-metering-mismatch-during-fallback-routing", "status": "In Progress", "date": "2025-07-20", "text": "- When fallback is taken, the usage events recorded in the metering pipeline reflect the pre-routing token estimate (or no additional increment) instead of the post-rendered token count produced by the actual model invocation.
- Result: per-key and per-org counters in the accounting DB (and downstream billing events) show fewer tokens than the model served. This affects quota enforcement (delayed throttles) and customer invoices.
Reproduction steps (deterministic within our staging environment):
1) Create staging org `acct-fallback-test` with per-route quota 1M tokens/month and route-level billing enabled.
2) Configure route `/chat/summary` to default to model M1 (tokenizer A) and allow fallback to M1-quant (tokenizer A, different kernel) and M2-small (tokenizer B) when latency SLOs exceed threshold.
3) Send a burst of 300 requests with long prompts designed to trigger fallback (use request pattern attached in `repro-requests.json` in Drive).
4) Observe routing traces in X-Ray (trace ids in reproducer). Confirm ~40% of requests were routed to fallback."}, {"source": "sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-208404-toolcall-aggregation-margin-invoice-breakdown-question.json", "chunk": "3/7", "kind": "Jira ticket", "title": "SUP-208404: Discrepancy: tool-invoke line items vs aggregated token lines producing ~12% higher May invoice", "status": "Resolved", "date": "2026-03-10", "text": "5) Run billing-aggregator for that hour window and inspect the output lines for duplication.
investigation_notes: Initial triage by Support (Laila) collected usage IDs and escalated to Billing Eng.
On 2026-03-06 Ravi reproduced locally using a synthetic stream that invoked an inline tool returning ~1k tokens; the postback pipeline generated two separate meter events: one for the tool_invoke (correct) and one for chat.tokens (incorrect).
Hypothesis: aggregator dedup logic uses (request_id, api_key) but not invocation_id for streaming postbacks—when streaming is cut into partial postbacks, the later chunk that contains the tool payload does not carry the dedupe flag and gets classified as chat tokens.
Query run: SELECT count(*) FROM meters WHERE invocation_id IS NOT NULL AND meter_type = 'chat.tokens.v1' AND created_at BETWEEN '2026-05-01' AND '2026-05-31' AND customer = 'neonretail' -> 4,312 lines.
Found a regression introduced by infra PR github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2621 which modified streaming postback composition to dedupe on request_id only (PR reverted in staging)."}, {"source": "sources/slack/support/1719504321-failover-served-incompatible-variant-billing-hiccup.json", "chunk": "2/5", "kind": "Slack thread", "title": "#support thread 1719504321-failover-served-incompatible-variant-billing-hiccup", "status": "n/a", "date": "2024-06-27", "text": "ops-bot: routing decision: fallback_policy=region_then_capacity; selected backup region=us-west-2; selected model_variant=invoice-parse-v2-lite (compatible_by_api but not by tokenizer/vocab).
jamal_eng: ah ok — variant is a lighter quantized family that uses a different tokenizer/vocab mapping. That's our mismatch. When we fallback we should prefer tokenizer-compatible variants or perform tokenizer translation.
ashley_support: customer also flagged billing: token billing showed sudden spike for the failed requests (they saw three increments for 1 call). billing-bot, do we have meters for that session?
billing-bot: meter snapshot for acct AcmePay: 1719504215 -> +0.8 units (attempt failed), 1719504221 -> +2.6 units (retry served by lite variant), 1719504230 -> +0.0 units (client retry aborted). Total billed: 3.4 units. Correlation id: rwd-req-3f9b.
jamal_eng: the lite variant has different tokenization rules; the client considered the output invalid and retried, so they paid extra. That’s bad."}]}

The **Hosted API usage line for Aug 1–15 was $1,301.46** on invoice **INV-BG-202608-009**. It’s open. The Aug 16–31 Hosted API line was $862.80, so the first half was higher.

The first-half line covers three request IDs, totaling about **41.6 million billed tokens**. All three usage records show HTTP 200, and the invoice check found no duplicate billing of those requests. That doesn’t establish exactly why the cost was higher: usage is recorded per server-admitted attempt, so client retries can add billable attempts, and streaming requests can incur prompt and generated tokens even if the stream is later cancelled. Higher request volume or longer prompts/responses could also contribute. The records don’t confirm which of those factors applied here.
So retry attempts are billed as usage as well?

{"query": "usage accounting retries server-admitted attempts each admitted attempt can be billable HTTP failures retry billing HTTP status rule hosted API", "results": [{"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/usage-accounting-retries-and-stream-cancellation.json", "chunk": "2/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Usage accounting: retries and streaming cancellation", "status": "published", "date": "2025-02-18", "text": "## Key definitions
- **Attempt**: a single request admitted by the Redwood API gateway (server-side).
- **Logical request**: what the customer thinks of as one user action; may map to multiple attempts if the client retries.
## What we bill
### Retries
- Redwood usage is recorded per-attempt.
- If a client retries after a timeout or non-200 response, each admitted attempt can be billable.
- The Usage dashboard lists rows by **request_id** (attempt identifier).
### Streaming cancellation
- **Prompt tokens** are counted once the request is admitted (even if the client cancels the stream later).
- **Completion tokens** are counted based on tokens actually generated/streamed prior to cancellation."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/overload-errors-and-retry-guidance.json", "chunk": "7/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API overload errors: support guidance, retry/backoff, and escalation", "status": "published", "date": "2025-12-05", "text": "(continued) ## Canonical mapping: status → meaning → what we tell customers
| HTTP | Typical meaning | What Support should say | Customer action |
|------|------------------|--------------------------|-----------------|
| 503 | Regional/model breaker open or load shedding | “Redwood is temporarily overloaded in the requested region/model. We are rejecting early to avoid timeouts and protect overall reliability.” | Respect Retry-After; backoff + jitter; optionally route to another region/model if configured; reduce max_tokens/streaming concurrency; retry with bounded attempts. |

- If the customer reports **timeouts** with no JSON error, treat as a separate issue (possible client/network or upstream timeouts) and escalate based on impact.

Streaming workloads can worsen overload if clients open many concurrent streams.

- If the customer can tolerate it, recommend **shorter outputs** (reduce `max_tokens`) and/or **shorter prompts**.
- If a stream fails mid-response with an overload error on reconnect attempts, advise them to back off and resume with a bounded number of attempts.
### What NOT to recommend
- “Just retry in a tight loop.”
- “Retry immediately with the same concurrency.”
- “Spin up many parallel retries to get through.”"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/usage-accounting-retries-and-stream-cancellation.json", "chunk": "3/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Usage accounting: retries and streaming cancellation", "status": "published", "date": "2025-02-18", "text": "## Common customer symptoms

4) For troubleshooting, ask for a small set of request_ids + the customers retry/cancel metrics."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/hosted-api-slo-overload-exceptions-and-budget-policy.json", "chunk": "4/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API SLO: Overload Exceptions and Error Budget Policy", "status": "published", "date": "2025-12-05", "text": "### “Explicit overload” requirement
For overload to be treated as “controlled” (and not as ambiguous failure), responses must include:
- A stable overload error code (see tables below)

If these are missing, SRE will classify as “generic failure” for incident reporting until corrected.
---
## Hosted API Availability SLO (current)
**Metric name (conceptual):** Hosted API Request Success Rate
**Objective:** 99.9% monthly availability (rolling 30 days) for paid Hosted tiers, measured at the API gateway.
**In-scope endpoints:**
- `/v1/chat/completions`
- `/v1/completions`

Yes. Redwood records usage per **server-admitted attempt**, so if a client retries after a timeout or non-200 response, each attempt that Redwood admits can be billable. A retry that is rejected before admission isn’t covered by that rule. For streaming, admitted prompt tokens are counted, and completion tokens reflect what was generated before cancellation.
